# The gap to Claude Fable 5.1

*Generated by `python -m r52.bar` on 2026-09-13. Published numbers retrieved 2026-09-13; every one carries a source URL and its eval conditions in `r52/bar/bar.yaml`.*

`—` means **no published number exists** — never 0. `†` marks a number our research flagged UNVERIFIED. `≡` marks a gap where both sides come from the **same evaluator**, which is the only kind of gap worth trusting. Superscripts are footnotes giving the eval conditions; the legend is at the bottom.

> **Read this first.** Three standing warnings from research/01 §6. (1) The harness is worth more than the model: flipping two API settings took GPT-5.6 Sol from 13.3% to 38.3% on ARC-AGI-3, same model. (2) Anthropic evaluates with production safeguards ON, scoring zero where a classifier fires, while comparison models run with them off -- published Claude scores understate raw capability. (3) Composite indices refit globally and are not comparable across versions: Artificial Analysis moved Fable 5.1 through 65.7 -> 57 -> 53 in two weeks for the same model.

## Classic local set

These are **dead at the frontier** — research/01 §1.4: not one of the nine September-2026 frontier launches reports SWE-bench Verified, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, AIME, LiveCodeBench, HumanEval or MATH-500. They are here because they are how *our* models get measured: a 124M model trained on a Mac Mini is nowhere near saturating any of them, and they run locally with no API key. Rows that are all `—` across the frontier columns are not gaps in this file — they are the honest state of the world.

## Our runs: targets, not results

Nothing has been measured yet, so every cell above for these models is an em dash. These are the acceptance criteria; `results/<run>/eval.json` fills the cells in.

| Model | Benchmark | Target | Where the target comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| r52-nano-30m | note | — | No target scores set; this run exists to validate the pipeline, not to beat a model. |
| r52-124m | fineweb-val-loss | <= 3.28 nats/token | docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §10; modded-nanogpt's speedrun target at the same parameter count |
| r52-124m | hellaswag | >= 29.4 % acc | docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §10; the GPT-2 124M reference |
| r52-124m | dclm-core | — | TO BE MEASURED BY US -- no published CORE score exists for GPT-2 small (124M); nanochat's leaderboard reference is GPT-2 XL (1.5B) at 0.256525. ARCHITECTURE §6 requires running our CORE port on HF gpt2 to establish the 124M reference before we can claim to beat it. |

## Saturation scorecard

From research/01 §7. The left column is where effort is wasted; the right column is where the headroom actually is.

| Saturated / dead | Near-saturated | Real headroom |
|---|---|---|
| **SWE-bench Verified** — contaminated; formally deprecated by OpenAI (Feb 2026) | **ARC-AGI-2** — 95.0%; 12+ configurations at >=88% | **OSWorld 2.0** — 31.4% binary ceiling |
| **ARC-AGI-1** — 98.5% > the 98.0% human panel | **MCP-Atlas** — 10 models within 8.9 points | **Remote Labor Index** — 15.8% ceiling |
| **Arena Text** — top 4 within 5 Elo, confidence intervals overlap | **GPQA Diamond** — top 10 within 1.9 points | **ARC-AGI-3 (standard harness)** — 62.7% |
| **AIME / OTIS Mock AIME** — 7 models at exactly 100.0%; explicitly retired by Anthropic | **SimpleBench** — 4 models above the human baseline | **Terminal-Bench 4.0** — 58.2% |
| **MATH Level 5** — 98.1%, abandoned | **Arena Document** — top 6 within 22 Elo | **HLE** — 54.8% ceiling on Scale's run |
| **MMLU / MMLU-Pro** — dropped by every 2026 launch |  | **EnigmaEval** — 39.3% |
| **OSWorld v1** — 86% |  | **Vending-Bench 2** — 4x below a competent human (~$63k) |
| **BrowseComp** — 92% |  | **FrontierMath Erdos** — 2.9% -- one model has solved any at all |
| **Aider Polyglot** — last update 2025-11-20 |  | **Harvey Legal Agent Bench** — 15.8% best all-criteria-pass |
| **BigCodeBench** — ~Apr 2025 |  |  |
| **LiveCodeBench official board** — window ends May 2025 |  |  |
| **MASK** — 7 models >90% |  |  |

research/01 §0: *"Every headline number in this report is a model + harness + effort level + grader tuple. Treat single numbers as meaningless without that tuple."* Each superscript below is that tuple.
